# Gramlot 0.3.8 — Bag trees and reusable page frames

A Bag-backed tree now supports lazy resolvers, icons, computed text or sanitized
structured HTML labels, label/node classes, `hideValues=False`, selection and
`autoCollapse`. Native internal drag and drop uses declarative eligibility,
named Logic callbacks and application-owned Data updates. External drops,
cross-browser-window transport and the remaining advanced legacy options are
outside this release.

`FramePage` provides five region hooks. `IndexPage` adds Bag navigation and
retained tab panels, with an iframe as the default panel. This replaces the old
fixed IndexPage shell: upgrade custom subclasses and the gallery together.
NavigationResolver keeps independent directory requests and caching; its shared
asynchronous cache no longer depends on a dataRemote NodeBinding. dataRemote
retains its published scheduling and synchronous contracts.

Drawer handles are visible at rest (6 px, 20% opacity), reveal on hover and
animate operator activation. Automatic visibility changes are immediate and
reduced-motion preferences are respected. Inspector colors follow the theme.

The repository guide GC-095 §110 documents Python-first sites, region hooks,
navigation Bags, nested routes, lazy directories, iframe panels and cleanup.
Database selectors, Genropy integration experiments and editor ports are excluded.

Qualification includes the full core suites, resolver lifecycle checks, inspector
tests and Chromium/WebKit tree, drawer, retained-iframe and internal-drop checks.
